title: Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
abstract: <jats:p>Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Education and Learning Technology

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
abstract:
<jats:p>Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored.
Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes.
Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement.
Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization.
Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
abstract: <jats:p>The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)

title: HYBRID NETWORK INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM BASED ON SIGNATURE ANALYSIS AND MACHINE LEARNING METHODS
abstract: <jats:p>In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.</jats:p>

title: Online Acceptance and Commitment Therapy With Contingency Management for Women With Methamphetamine Use Disorder: Mixed Methods Feasibility Study.
abstract: Methamphetamine use disorder (MUD) is an escalating public health concern that disproportionately affects women and gender-diverse individuals and is frequently accompanied by trauma exposure and psychiatric comorbidity. Evidence-based psychosocial treatments remain limited, particularly interventions that are feasible, scalable, and responsive to these intersecting vulnerabilities. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary outcomes of an online acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) group intervention combined with contingency management (CM) for individuals with MUD, with a primary focus on women and gender-diverse participants. A single-arm, open-label feasibility trial was conducted with 61 (n=57, 93% women; n=4, 7% gender-diverse; mean age 39.8, SD 9.4 years) participants. The intervention comprised 15 online ACT group sessions delivered over 8 weeks, preceded by an individual motivational interviewing session, and supported by CM to reinforce session attendance. Primary outcomes were methamphetamine use (grams and days) assessed using the timeline follow-back method. Secondary outcomes included anxiety, depression, and trauma symptoms, psychological flexibility, craving, functional impairment, and quality of life. Changes over time were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models under an intention-to-treat framework. Effect sizes were calculated using standardized mean change relative to baseline. Postintervention, individual semistructured interviews were conducted via videoconferencing with all completers to evaluate satisfaction and perceived active ingredients of the intervention. Transcripts were analyzed using software-supported thematic analysis, and the themes were refined through discussions with the research team. Retention was moderate, with 50 participants attending at least 1 session and 30 completing the intervention (≥10 sessions). Significant reductions in methamphetamine use occurred across all timeline follow-back measures and were maintained at the 1-month follow-up. Significant improvements were observed in anxiety, depression, trauma symptoms, and psychological flexibility. Craving and quality-of-life domains did not show significant changes after correction. Qualitative thematic analysis revealed high acceptability across 4 primary themes. Participants emphasized emotional connection, normalization of experiences, and mutual accountability as key drivers of engagement, active monitoring of use, values-based reflection, and mindfulness tools useful for coping with cravings. They also highlighted platform convenience, a safe women-focused composition, and the role of financial incentives as external motivators supporting clinical adherence. Constructive requests were made for additional trauma-focused content and emotional literacy. This online ACT protocol combined with CM appears feasible and acceptable for women and gender-diverse individuals with MUD and was associated with meaningful reductions in methamphetamine use and improvements in psychological functioning. While these preliminary results are limited by a single-arm design, a relatively short follow-up period, and reliance on self-report measures, they provide a strong foundation for future research. These findings support further evaluation of the integrated ACT+CM protocol in larger randomized controlled trials to assess long-term efficacy and help to close critical digital health treatment gaps for this population.

title: Verification Behavior and Metacognitive Calibration in AI-Assisted Clinical Reasoning Among Physiotherapy Students: Cross-Sectional, 3-Group Comparative Study.
abstract: Generative AI is part of everyday study in the health professions. Safe use is thought to depend less on how much students use it than on how they handle its output: checking it, reasoning soundly when it is wrong, and keeping confidence aligned with accuracy. Which behaviors are associated with better performance is untested in physiotherapy education. We tested (1) whether status in a structured "AI in Healthcare" elective (no course exposure, currently taking, or completed) was associated with performance on a clinical case examination (basic knowledge, case-based reasoning, and hallucination-trap items) and with metacognitive calibration, and (2) among students who used AI during the examination, whether self-reported cross-checking of AI output or the quantity of AI use was associated with performance. In this cross-sectional study, 137 (71%) of the 193 invited physiotherapy students (no course exposure: n=67; currently taking: n=43; completed: n=27) completed a researcher-developed 30-item open-resource examination with item-level confidence ratings and an AI-use survey (cross-check frequency; number of AI-assisted questions). Prespecified primary outcomes were the hallucination-trap score, case-based reasoning, and the calibration gap. The per-participant Brier score was the confirmatory calibration test. Group contrasts used Kruskal-Wallis tests and heteroscedasticity-consistent regression adjusted for age, year, grade point average, and prior AI use. Among 108 AI users, cross-check frequency and AI-use quantity were modeled jointly, then adjusted for demographics, course group, and basic-knowledge score. Cross-check frequency was associated with total score (β=2.98, 95% CI 1.27-4.68; P<.001), persisted after adjustment for demographics and course group (β=2.81, 95% CI 1.26-4.36; P<.001) and after excluding fast completions, and attenuated once basic-knowledge score was added (fully adjusted β=1.08, 95% CI -0.09 to 2.24; P=.07). AI-use quantity was not positively associated with performance (β=-0.26, 95% CI -0.53 to 0.00; P=.05). Calibration differed by group on the per-participant Brier score (H In an open-resource clinical examination, performance was associated with how students verified AI output, not how much they used it. The clearest deficit was metacognitive calibration rather than accuracy. These prespecified associations identify verification behavior and confidence calibration as measurable candidate targets for AI-literacy instruction. Because the design is cross-sectional and verification was self-reported, their instructional value requires testing in randomized or longitudinal designs.

title: A spatial peroxisomal switch of AGPS drives ether lipid-induced ferroptosis in vascular calcification.
abstract: Vascular calcification is a life-threatening complication of chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet the metabolic changes that cause blood vessels to harden remain unclear. We found that the pathologically enhanced relocation of a lipid-producing enzyme, alkylglycerone phosphate synthase (AGPS), into cellular compartments called peroxisomes acts as a critical driver of this disease. This spatial shift, triggered by the protein PKCη (protein kinase C η), causes a surge in specific lipids that promote cell death and mineral buildup in the vessels. To disrupt this destructive process, we used generative artificial intelligence (AI) to design a custom peptide that blocks the interaction between AGPS and PKCη. When delivered systemically using lipid nanoparticles, this AI-designed therapeutic successfully prevented the enzyme's excessive relocation, stopped toxic lipid accumulation, and profoundly reduced aortic calcification in CKD mice. Our findings uncover a crucial metabolic trigger for vascular calcification and highlight AI-guided nanotherapeutics as a promising strategy for treating vascular diseases.

title: Physics-embedded neural spectral wave model.
abstract: Simulating ocean surface waves is essential for understanding Earth's climate and marine environments, but numerical wave models solving directional wave spectrum remain computationally prohibitive for climate applications. Data-driven deep learning approaches struggle to capture wave physics with high dimensionality, failing to generalize beyond their training domains. To bridge this divide, we present the neural spectral wave model (NeuralSWM), a hybrid physics-AI framework. By embedding a differentiable numerical solver to govern universal wave propagation alongside a neural network that learns complex energy source terms, NeuralSWM efficiently simulates full directional wave spectra. The model demonstrates true zero-shot transferability: Trained exclusively on wind-sea dominated semienclosed South China Sea, it can simulate wave dynamics across the swell-dominated Eastern Tropical Pacific and the high-wind, long-fetch regimes of the Southern Indian Ocean. Validated against satellite altimetry, NeuralSWM maintains high accuracy (∼96% of the performance) at a fraction of traditional computational costs, providing a scalable foundation for integrating explicit wave dynamics into global Earth system models.

title: Principles of locus-specific chromatin remodeling induced by therapeutic DNA integration.
abstract: Understanding how integrated genetic elements engage host chromatin is essential for improving gene-therapy safety. Lentiviral vectors (LVs) are widely used, yet how integrated cis-regulatory elements (CREs) interact with the three-dimensional (3D) host genome remains poorly understood. Here, we performed a systematic, locus-resolved analysis of chromatin accessibility, 3D genome organization, and transcriptional output at 329 precisely mapped LV integration sites. LV integration locally remodels chromatin by increasing accessibility, inducing transcriptional read-through, and generating aberrant host-LV fusion transcripts in a strongly site- and orientation-dependent manner, establishing orientation as a key determinant of regulatory impact and a structural basis for locus-specific genotoxic risk. Incorporating chromatin insulator elements stabilizes transgene expression while preserving topologically associating domains and global architecture. We further developed a machine learning framework that prioritizes integration sites by predicted regulatory perturbation across cell-type-specific chromatin contexts. Together, these findings define principles by which ectopic CREs reshape local genome function and inform safer therapeutic genome integration.

title: Interpretable Continuous Glucose Monitoring Patterns of Type 1 and Type 2 Diabetes Across Cohorts and Sensors: Development and External Validation Study.
abstract: Distinguishing type 1 diabetes (T1D) from type 2 diabetes (T2D) guides treatment, but adult presentations overlap. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) captures day-to-day glucose patterns, but CGM studies differ in recruitment, treatment, and sensor manufacturer, complicating classifier evaluation. We tested whether 7-day CGM features distinguish source-labeled T1D, T2D, and no diabetes in adults when entire datasets are held out, compared interpretable and neural models with simple baselines, and measured how sensor substitution changes predictions. We trained models on 4 adult datasets (AI-READI, ShanghaiT2DM, T1DiabetesGranada, and T1DEXI) and tested them on 4 others (Glucotypes, ShanghaiT1DM, AZT1D, and CGMacros), with every T1D/T2D-by-Dexcom/Abbott combination in both partitions. A cap of 100 participants per dataset and diagnosis yielded 492 training and 107 test participants. Each 7-day window provided 47 CGM features; predictions were averaged within participant. We compared mean-glucose and clinical-summary (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, and glucose zones) logistic regression with elastic net, boosted trees, and 4 neural networks. The primary end point was participant-level macro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) with bootstrap 95% CIs. In 29 CGMacros participants wearing Abbott FreeStyle Libre Pro and Dexcom G6 Pro sensors simultaneously, we substituted Dexcom for Libre input. Among the 107 test participants (37 with T1D, 18 with T2D, and 52 without diabetes), elastic net achieved a macro-AUROC of 0.943 (95% CI 0.914-0.969) and a T1D-versus-T2D AUROC of 0.935 (95% CI 0.869-0.980), exceeding mean-glucose and clinical-summary logistic regression (paired gains over the latter 0.046, 95% CI 0.015-0.079, and 0.105, 95% CI 0.017-0.212). Pooled mean glucose was similar (T1D-minus-T2D difference 5.28 mg/dL, 95% CI -1.24 to 11.40), whereas the mean of daily differences (MODD), the leading elastic-net feature, was higher in T1D (21.11 mg/dL, 95% CI 18.31-23.83). T1D sensitivity was 78.4% overall, 92% in AZT1D, and 50% in ShanghaiT1DM; T2D precision was 45.7%. No dataset contained both T1D and T2D; when the T1D-versus-T2D contrast came from the shared Shanghai registry and sensor, elastic-net AUROC was 0.82-0.86; the 47 features also separated 2 T1D Dexcom cohorts, T1DEXI and AZT1D (AUROC 0.998, 95% CI 0.994-1.000). Clinical-summary logistic regression led within Shanghai (0.907 vs 0.859) and in Abbott-only evaluation (0.976 vs 0.887). Substituting Dexcom for Libre input reduced primary elastic-net log loss by 0.389 (95% CI 0.140-0.673) but increased Abbott-only log loss by 0.567 (95% CI 0.257-0.923). In primary external testing, an interpretable 47-feature elastic-net model discriminated diabetes categories better than mean-glucose and clinical-summary baselines, with day-to-day glucose variability as the leading signal; because diagnosis and cohort coincided, this result may be optimistic. T1D errors concentrated in 1 adult-onset cohort, and sensor substitution changed predictions depending on the training setting, so classifiers pooling manufacturers should also be checked with paired-sensor recordings.

title: Externally Validated Explainable Machine Learning for Identifying High Death Anxiety in Chronic Heart Failure: Multicentre Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: To develop and externally validate explainable machine-learning models for identifying high death anxiety among patients with chronic heart failure. A multicentre cross-sectional study with external validation. Hospitalised patients with chronic heart failure were recruited from four hospitals in China. The development cohort included 450 inpatients from three hospitals in Henan, Jilin, and Beijing, and the independent external validation cohort included 200 inpatients from a different tertiary hospital in Henan. Twenty-seven predictors were used to develop three machine-learning models. Discrimination, calibration, exploratory net benefit, and model explanations were assessed. The primary extreme gradient boosting model showed strong external discrimination but imperfect calibration. Random forest had higher discrimination, and machine learning showed no clear discrimination advantage over logistic regression. Model explanations identified fear of disease progression, activities of daily living, hope, sleep duration, and self-esteem as the most influential predictors. Explainable machine-learning models may support the identification of patients with chronic heart failure who have high death anxiety and may assist targeted psychological assessment. Prospective evaluation should compare model-assisted assessment with direct measurement of death anxiety. This study shows that multidomain information collected during patient assessment can be integrated using explainable machine learning to identify concurrent high Death Anxiety Scale scores. Such an approach may have clinical value when relevant information is already available, but it requires prospective comparison with direct Death Anxiety Scale assessment. Reporting followed the Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis Or Diagnosis plus Artificial Intelligence guideline. This study did not include patient or public involvement in its design, conduct, analysis, interpretation, or reporting.

title: Effect of Steady Flow Amplitude on Hemodynamics at Transverse-Sigmoid Sinus Junction in Pulsatile Tinnitus.
abstract: Pulsatile tinnitus (PT) induced by sigmoid sinus wall dehiscence (SSWD) combined with diverticulum severely reduces patients' quality of life. Hemodynamic disturbances at the transverse-sigmoid sinus (TS-SS) junction exert crucial pathogenic effects on PT. However, the influence of steady flow amplitude remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effect of changes in steady flow amplitude on hemodynamic parameters at the TS-SS junction in PT patients. Case series. Tertiary Academic Center. Patient-specific venous models of three PT patients were reconstructed from clinical imaging. Nine flow conditions were established: baseline and steady flow amplitude adjustments of ±20%, ±40%, ±60%, and ±80%. Transient computational fluid dynamics was used to quantify blood flow patterns, wall pressure, and wall shear stress (WSS) at the TS-SS junction. Reduced steady flow amplitude attenuated flow disturbance on the SSWD region, shrank high-pressure and high-WSS zones, and reduced average/maximum pressure (  This study identifies steady flow amplitude as a vital hemodynamic regulator at the TS-SS junction, providing novel quantitative evidence to clarify PT pathophysiological mechanisms. Modulating steady flow amplitude may improve abnormal hemodynamic on the SSWD region, offering a potential targeted therapeutic strategy for PT patients.

title: Mechanisms of mindfulness in early-stage Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) progresses gradually across early clinical stages, during which compensatory neural mechanisms may remain responsive to behavioral intervention. Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) are increasingly studied in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) due to AD and mild AD dementia (early-stage AD), yet most prior reviews emphasize clinical efficacy rather than underlying mechanisms. Here, we review behavioral, neuroimaging, and electrophysiological findings in early-stage AD and propose a multi-level mechanistic model through which mindfulness may influence cognition. Across heterogeneous protocols, MBIs show modest, domain-specific benefits, most consistently in attention and recognition memory. Mechanistic data, though limited, converge on strengthened connectivity between hippocampal and posterior cingulate regions, improved coordination within large-scale attention and control networks, millisecond-scale changes in attention- and encoding-related brain responses, and reduced stress-related markers (i.e., hair cortisol and cortisone). We integrate these findings into a temporally ordered, dose-dependent model in which mindfulness practice may strengthen attention, conflict monitoring, and stress regulation, potentially enhancing communication between memory systems (related to default mode network hubs) and frontoparietal executive control networks. We propose that with sustained practice, such functional changes may contribute to downstream structural preservation in hippocampal and frontoparietal regions. Within this model, MBIs may serve as low-risk, mechanistically informed adjuncts to disease-modifying and lifestyle interventions in early-stage AD. Effects likely vary by stage, from augmenting compensatory processes in MCI to supporting everyday function in mild AD dementia. Future longitudinal trials should incorporate biomarker-confirmed diagnoses, higher practice doses, standardized cognitive outcomes, and multimodal neural assessments.

title: GenAI for Head and Neck Tumor Board Decision Support: Blinded Comparison of Retrieval Augmentation.
abstract: To evaluate large language model (LLM) performance in multidisciplinary tumor board (MTB) decision support for head and neck cancer (HNC). Blinded comparative study. Single tertiary academic center using real-world tumor board cases. One hundred de-identified HNC cases were transcribed from institutional MTB presentation materials. GPT-4 and GPT-5 outputs, generated with and without in-context guideline grounding (RAG) using National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) 2025 guidelines, were evaluated by five blinded fellowship-trained head and neck surgeons. Outputs were scored across five domains: staging accuracy, treatment recommendation accuracy, prognosis accuracy, guideline adherence, and overall clinical usefulness using a five-point Likert scale with predefined anchors. Mixed-effects regression models accounted for clustering by case and reviewer. All configurations demonstrated high performance, with composite scores >4.45/5. GPT-5 without RAG achieved the highest mean score (4.82), followed by GPT-4 without RAG (4.55), GPT-5 with RAG (4.53), and GPT-4 with RAG (4.45). Configurations without RAG outperformed those with RAG (Δ = 0.22, P < .001), and GPT-5 outperformed GPT-4 (Δ = 0.15, P = .008). Mixed-effects modeling confirmed a significant effect of model version (β = .17, P = .001), while RAG was not associated with improved performance (β = -.06, P = .25); a negative model-by-RAG interaction did not reach significance (β = -.13, P = .07). LLMs demonstrate strong expert-rated performance in HNC tumor board decision support. However, naïve guideline-based RAG was associated with lower performance, suggesting that poorly optimized retrieval may introduce irrelevant context in complex decision-making. These findings underscore retrieval design as a critical determinant of safe clinical AI deployment and reinforce the need for clinician oversight.
